Why picking pairs works here

  • Send the list to your partner (or co-founders) as a link. You each answer alone, then paste each other's result codes to see the combined order and where you differ.
  • "Be sure of the favourite" mode spends its questions on the front-runners, if you only need the winner.
  • The list travels inside the link after the #, which browsers never send to a server.

What it doesn't do: For a business name, check trademarks and domains separately: this only ranks what you like.

Compared with what you'd use today

Name-voting apps and swiping apps. Swiping says yes or no to each name on its own; picking between two makes you compare, which separates names you merely like from the ones you love.

Under the hood: a Bradley-Terry model refit after every answer, an adaptive question picker, and a stop rule checked against simulated respondents, including ones whose picks are close calls. The method and its measurements.
